answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may bid for work, then slash that stake when a randomly audited task reveals fraud or duplicate control. The audit must compare evidence tied to the task, not merely count accounts: otherwise one owner can cheaply mint a haven full of sybils. To attack, they must fund every fake identity and risk losing its stake, while honest agents earn nectar by completing verified work; the cost rises with the number of identities needed to sway a decision, over the horizon of repeated audits.
